blockingProblems: LINE 93, THE CENTRAL ARGUMENT IS LOGICALLY INVALID. 'A feedforward network with smooth activations is a composition of affine maps and smooth nonlinearities. It is infinitely differentiable in its inputs and in its parameters... It cannot be made non-analytic.' This derives analyticity from smoothness. C-infinity does not imply C-omega; the standard counterexample, exp(-1/x^2) glued to zero, is smooth everywhere and analytic nowhere at the origin. The chapter has spent five sections building exactly this distinction (line 7 'the intermolecular potential is smooth', line 77 'Z_N is entire... ln Z_N is real-analytic') and then collapses it at the hinge where the book's thesis is stated. A referee at Cambridge, Princeton or Oxford stops here.

LINE 93, THE DERIVATIVE BOUND IS FALSE AS STATED. 'every one of its derivatives is bounded on any bounded domain by products of weight norms and activation Lipschitz constants.' A Lipschitz constant bounds the FIRST derivative only. Second and higher derivatives of a composition require bounds on the corresponding higher derivatives of the activation (Faa di Bruno), which no Lipschitz constant supplies. As written this is a graduate-level error delivered in the cadence of a proof.

LINES 91-99, THE ENTIRE CLOSING SECTION CITES NOBODY. The chapter characterises 'a large and growing literature' (line 91), describes its protocol in specific detail ('the temperature at which its output crosses one half is reported as an estimate of T_c'), and then attacks it, without one reference. The ch01 packet contains zero machine-learning verifiedClaims, so nothing here is traceable to the packet. Under the stated evidentiary rule that is disqualifying on its own; independent of the rule, no university press permits a book to litigate against an unnamed literature. The protocol described is recognisably specific published work. Either cite it or do not assert it.

LINES 93-95, INTERNAL CONTRADICTION AT THE THESIS. Line 93 says the network is defective because it 'excludes non-analyticity by construction.' Line 95 then concedes the training data comes from 'a system whose free energy is analytic everywhere.' By the chapter's own proof at line 77 the finite-lattice target IS analytic. Model and target are therefore matched, not mismatched, and the claim at line 95 that 'the mismatch is doubled' is precisely backwards. There is a real argument nearby, about extrapolation to a limit neither object contains, but the chapter states the wrong one and never resolves the tension.

LINE 53, THE FAILURE OF LANDAU THEORY IS ASSERTED AND NEVER EXPLAINED. 'It assumes that the free energy is an analytic function of the order parameter at the transition, which is precisely the assumption that fails there.' Why does it fail? Fluctuations on all scales once xi diverges, mean field exact only at or above the upper critical dimension four, the Ginzburg criterion: none of it appears. The packet supplies exactly this in the unused Wilson-Fisher claim ('d = 4 - epsilon... about the upper critical dimension four, where mean-field theory becomes exact'). A graduate student finishes the section knowing mean field is wrong and not knowing why.

LINE 85, THE FINITE-SIZE PEAK FORMULA DEGENERATES ON THE CHAPTER'S OWN SHOWPIECE. 'a peak of finite height growing as L^{alpha/nu}'. For the 2D Ising model, given a full section at line 57, alpha = 0 and the specific heat diverges logarithmically. L^0 = constant is the wrong answer; the correct scaling is log L. The one worked case the reader has been taught is the case where the stated formula silently fails.

LINES 81-87, THE FINITE-SIZE SCALING SECTION IS WHOLLY UNCITED. Peak height L^{alpha/nu}, shift of order L^{-1/nu}, first-order rounding of order 1/N, and the ansatz-fitting critique at line 87 are bare assertion. This is the section the chapter itself calls 'the fact that the rest of this book is organized around' (line 71). Nothing in the packet supports any of it; Fisher's 1974 Reviews of Modern Physics review sits unused.

LINE 33, THE BKT PARAGRAPH IS UNMOTIVATED BECAUSE MERMIN-WAGNER IS OMITTED. The chapter says the transition is 'driven by the unbinding of vortex and antivortex pairs' but never says what conventional order is impossible in two dimensions or why a topological mechanism is needed. The packet supplies the missing premise verbatim: 'This theorem is the obstacle that the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless mechanism circumvents, since BKT order is topological rather than conventional.' The fix was in hand and unused.

LINE 17, G AND MU ARE SILENTLY CONFLATED. The argument is set up on 'the Gibbs free energy G(T,p) of a homogeneous phase' with S and V as its first derivatives, i.e. extensive G. Coexistence is then written 'mu_liq(T,p) = mu_vap(T,p)' with no statement that G/N = mu for a single-component system. In the chapter meant to teach the geometry of coexistence with maximum care, the one step where extensive and intensive potentials swap places is the step that is skipped.

LINES 47 AND 61, THE EXPONENTS ARE LISTED TWICE AND NEVER USED. Landau's mean-field values (beta = 1/2, gamma = 1, delta = 3, alpha = 0) appear at line 47; the scaling relations alpha + 2beta + gamma = 2 and gamma = beta(delta - 1) appear at line 61. The chapter never checks one against the other, though it takes one clause (0 + 1 + 1 = 2; 1 = (1/2)(3-1)). Nor does it give Onsager's nu = 1 or gamma = 7/4. So when nu is introduced at line 65 and made load-bearing at lines 81-85, the reader has never been given a single numerical value for it.
styleViolations: MECHANICAL CHECKS ARE CLEAN, AND I VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: zero U+2014 em dashes, zero U+2013 en dashes, zero occurrences of '--', zero bullet or numbered lists in the body, no end-of-chapter summary or recap. The chapter passes the non-negotiable formatting rules outright. The failures below are prose and apparatus, not formatting.

STRUCTURAL TIC, the 'two things' scaffold three times: line 5 'Two features of that observation carry most of the argument of this book', line 21 'Two things follow that are worth flagging now', line 55 'Two things are in that result, and both are load-bearing.' The reader starts hearing the machinery instead of the argument.

'WORTH' AS HEDGE-CUM-SIGNPOST three times: line 21 'worth flagging now', line 31 'it is worth being careful too', line 87 'It is also worth noticing what it does.' All three are throat-clearing that deletes without loss.

LINE 97, TRIPLE HEDGE AT THE CLIMAX. 'It is possible that the crossing point tracks the finite-size crossover... It is possible that it tracks something else... It is also possible that the architecture's own biases supply the extrapolation.' Three possibilities, no adjudication, no evidence, no preference. This is the paragraph the chapter has been driving toward and it declines to hold a position.
LINE 91, 'which is what a large and growing literature does.' The deadest phrase in academic writing, and here it stands in for the citation that should be there.

THE CLOSING QUESTION IS ASKED THREE TIMES: line 7 ('a stranger enterprise than it usually appears'), line 97 ('Something is being estimated. The question is what'), line 99 ('It is to ask what quantity the number is an estimate of'). Lines 97 and 99 are the same sentence twice. The ending is not flat, and it does leave the reader curious, but restatement blunts it and the final paragraph adds nothing its predecessor did not say.

LINE 71, 'it takes four lines to prove.' The proof runs six sentences over five lines plus a displayed equation. Small, but the chapter's authority rests on precisely this kind of precision and the flourish does not check out.

LINE 18, 'This is the whole mechanism, and it deserves to be stated plainly because everything later is a variation on it.' Announcing that a thing deserves to be stated plainly instead of stating it plainly.
LINES 23-33, the ladder metaphor is worked ten times across eleven lines ('ladder' four times, 'rung' six). Coherent, but at that density it stops being illustration and becomes a tic.

CITATION APPARATUS IS NOT PRESS-READY. Line 101, 'Citations used in this chapter', followed by sixteen entries carrying bare https://doi.org/ strings. No university press sets DOIs as visible URLs in end-matter. This is a working bibliography, not a book's notes, and it reads as one.
factProblems: THE VERIFIABLE CITATION LAYER IS IN GOOD ORDER AND ALL FIVE PACKET CORRECTIONS WERE CHECKED INDIVIDUALLY AND ALL FIVE APPLIED. Sauer is dated 2017 with EPJ Special Topics 226, 539-549 at lines 25 and 105, not the packet's uncorrected 2016. Rushbrooke's 1963 inequality is credited as PRECEDING Widom at line 61, with a separate Rushbrooke entry added at line 112, correcting the packet's chronologically wrong 'later'. The Berezinskii Russian original is given as ZhETF 59(3), 907-920, 1970 at line 116, not 1971. The Ehrenfest editorial gloss follows the correction's 'safer wording' almost exactly at line 31, including the concession that the framework 'proved fruitful and remains a standard entry point'. The Turnbull / fabricated 'John Chipman Fisher' correction and the 2021 Nobel correction concern material absent from this chapter, so they are moot here rather than violated. Every named person, paper, year and venue in the body traces to a verifiedClaim, including the traps: Lenz credited with the model and Ising only with the one-dimensional solution (line 57), the Ising-disproved-2D myth explicitly avoided, beta = 1/8 attributed to Yang 1952 with Onsager's unpublished 1948 announcement acknowledged, and Berezinskii's priority stated (line 33).

THE ENTIRE FINAL THIRD IS OUTSIDE THE PACKET. Lines 81-99, covering finite-size rounding, the L^{alpha/nu} and L^{-1/nu} forms, the 1/N first-order rounding, the finite-size-scaling-as-ansatz critique, and every claim about neural networks and the machine-learning literature, has no traceable source in verifiedClaims. That is roughly a third of the chapter and it contains the thesis.

UNSOURCED QUANTITATIVE ASSERTIONS IN THE OPENING. Line 3, '373 kelvin' and 'Roughly two and a quarter megajoules per kilogram'; line 5, 'The density of the material falls by three orders of magnitude across the transition.' I checked all three and all three are correct (373.15 K at 1 atm; L_vap approximately 2.257 MJ/kg; rho_liq/rho_vap approximately 1600). They are not fabrications. But they carry no note, and in a monograph the first three numbers a reader meets need one.

LINE 25, 'By the early 1930s the low-temperature laboratories had produced transitions that plainly were not like boiling.' Historical framing that motivates the whole Ehrenfest section, with no source. Line 29's lambda-point divergence is at least glancingly supported by the packet's correction text; this sentence is not.

LINE 31, ATTRIBUTION CREEP ONTO SAUER. 'Sauer's commentary is careful on this point and it is worth being careful too: the classification was not so much refuted as found to be describing a category with no typical members.' The colon places the author's own formulation directly behind Sauer's name. The packet records only that Sauer notes the lambda-point divergence forced modification and argues the framework 'remains important'. The gloss is defensible; the syntax lends it Sauer's authority.

LINE 19, the Clausius-Clapeyron relation dp/dT = L/(T*Delta V) is derived in text rather than cited, which is legitimate, but the derivation is compressed to 'Differentiating the coexistence condition along the curve gives', which is not a derivation. Show the two lines or cite it.
whatWouldMakeItAAA:
The first five sections are genuinely good and would survive a blind comparison against Goldenfeld or Cardy. The opening image earns its place, the Gibbs envelope argument at line 17 ("Analyticity is not lost by any single phase. It is lost by the operation of taking a minimum over phases") is the best sentence in the chapter and is a real explanation rather than a gesture, and the four-line finite-N analyticity proof at line 77 is clean and correctly reasoned. Citation discipline is better than most published books manage, and every packet correction was actually applied. The chapter fails on its last third, which is also the third the book depends on.

Six things would fix it. First, repair line 93. Smoothness does not imply analyticity, and the sentence as written is a category error committed in a chapter about that exact category. Say instead that the standard activations (tanh, sigmoid, softplus, erf-based GELU) are real-analytic and that a finite composition of analytic maps is analytic, which is true and is the argument the author meant. Then confront the fact that most of the literature under attack uses ReLU, which IS non-analytic, and explain why piecewise linearity still cannot produce a divergence. As it stands the strongest objection to the thesis is never raised. Second, delete the Lipschitz clause or replace it with a correct statement about bounded higher derivatives of the activation. Third, resolve the contradiction between lines 93 and 95. The honest claim is not that model and data mismatch; it is that model and data MATCH in analyticity and the reported quantity lives in neither, which is a sharper and more unsettling point than the one currently made. Fourth, cite the machine-learning literature by name, or commission packet entries so it can be cited; a monograph does not attack "a large and growing literature." Fifth, spend two hundred words explaining WHY Landau's analyticity assumption fails, using the Wilson-Fisher material already sitting unused in the packet, and give nu = 1 and gamma = 7/4 for Onsager so the exponent carrying lines 81-85 has a value attached. Sixth, cut one of lines 97 and 99 and commit to a position. The triple "it is possible that" is the sound of an author who has found a real problem and is afraid to say what he thinks about it. A chapter ending on a question is right; a chapter ending on three unranked hypotheses is a chapter that has not finished thinking.

Smaller: retire the "two things" scaffold in two of its three appearances, state G/N = mu at line 17, note that alpha = 0 turns L^{alpha/nu} into log L at line 85, put Mermin-Wagner into line 33 so the BKT paragraph has a premise, and convert the bibliography to press-format notes without bare URLs. With the ReLU objection answered and the Landau failure actually explained, this would be an excellent opening chapter. As it stands it is a very well written first two-thirds attached to a thesis that does not survive inspection.
